criterion: The ground, the panels, the wells, the dividers and the three levels of text across the workbench hold to one neutral family.
evaluation_rule: The workbench is the signed-in application: its rail, its event field and the surfaces beside them. Yes if every one of those chrome surfaces reads as a shade of one neutral family. No if any chrome surface carries a saturated hue of its own.

criterion: One accent blue marks what is interactive across the workbench, a green marks an increase, a red marks an error, an orange marks an approaching allowance, and a cyan marks a neutral notice.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a single blue appears on the primary action, the focus ring, the selection edge and links alone, and the four meaning colours each appear for their one meaning. No if the accent decorates a surface that does nothing, or one of the four meaning colours appears for a second meaning.

criterion: Series, variants and event classes on the event field draw from eight hues ordered for the greatest distance between any two.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a chart or a field overlay with several categories uses eight distinguishable hues before falling back to an ordered lightness ramp with direct labels. No if a ninth category repeats the first hue.

criterion: Numbers across the workbench sit on lining numerals of equal width so a column of figures lines up.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the digits in a numeric column sit in a straight vertical line and hold their width while a value updates. No if the digits drift out of alignment or the column shifts width as a number changes.

criterion: Corners across the workbench are barely softened, and depth is carried by a paired border and shadow.
evaluation_rule: Yes if rows, cards, popovers and sheets read as an instrument with near-square corners, each level of depth drawn with a border beside its shadow. No if surfaces are heavily rounded, or depth is drawn with a shadow alone on the dark ground.

criterion: The workbench is committed to a dark ground, with a light theme carrying every role at the same contrast.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the default appearance is a dark ground and switching to the light theme keeps every colour role legible. No if only one theme exists, or the light theme loses the meaning of a colour role.

criterion: An increase or a decrease anywhere in the workbench carries a glyph and a sign beside its hue.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every change figure shows an arrow or a sign as well as a colour, and every icon-only control carries a readable name. No if a reader who cannot tell the two hues apart would lose the direction of a change.

criterion: Moving the viewport of the event field leaves one history entry once the movement settles.
evaluation_rule: Yes if pressing the browser back control after panning and zooming returns to the previous place the viewport settled rather than stepping through every intermediate position. No if back steps through the movement one frame at a time.

criterion: The share sheet opens with the most restrictive setting already chosen, stating in one sentence what the recipient will see.
evaluation_rule: A share sheet is the panel that mints a read-only link on a saved insight. Yes if it opens with drilling down and person identifiers both switched off and a short expiry already selected, and carries one sentence describing the recipient's view. No if it opens with a wider scope, or describes the recipient's view nowhere.

criterion: The processing switch states which capabilities become unavailable before anybody enables the switch.
evaluation_rule: The processing switch is the setting that keeps every analysis on the owner's own store. Yes if the loss is written out beside the switch while the switch is still off. No if the capabilities disappear first and the owner discovers the loss afterwards.

criterion: A surface falling back to a narrower computation says so where the owner is reading.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a coarser resolution, a cached answer or an approximate match is stated on the surface that shows the result. No if a surface quietly serves the weaker answer with the same presentation as the full one.

criterion: Opening the insights surface beside the event field narrows the field, keeping the same visible time range.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the field keeps drawing beside the new surface and the span it shows before and after the mount is the same span. No if the field is torn down, or the visible time range changes because the field got narrower.

criterion: Releasing a held workspace resolves a conflict in the background, telling the owner afterwards.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the release completes with the conflict recorded in a list the owner can read later. No if a dialog stops the release to demand a choice at the moment connectivity returns.

criterion: A list filtered down to nothing names the filter responsible rather than reading as an empty list.
evaluation_rule: Yes if filtering a populated list to zero rows produces wording that names the filter, different from the wording shown when the list has never held anything. No if both states read the same.

criterion: A number on the workbench that changes counts through its intermediate values with its width fixed from the first frame.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a metric that updates runs through the values between the old figure and the new one, with the layout around it holding still. No if the number swaps in one step, or the layout shifts as the digits change.

criterion: Flicking the event field carries the movement on to a settle, and the field resists at the ends of the archive.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a fast drag keeps moving after the pointer is released and slows to rest, and dragging past the oldest event meets resistance that returns the view. No if the field stops dead when the pointer stops, or slides past the archive with a hard stop.

criterion: Under the reduced-motion preference the cohort dimming and the progress rail both remain after movement is removed.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a brushed cohort still dims the marks outside it and a long operation still shows a filling rail when reduced motion is on. No if either signal disappears along with the animation.

criterion: The event field announces its settled viewport as text naming the span, the event count and the person count.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a screen reader reaches a live description that states the time span on screen with how many events and how many people are in it. No if the field exposes only a canvas with nothing readable.

criterion: One keystroke opens a complete table of the rows the event field is drawing.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the table reached from the field holds the same rows the field draws rather than a summary of them. No if the table is a reduced subset, or nothing opens from the keyboard.

criterion: Narrowing the viewport collapses the rail beside the event field to icons with nothing overflowing sideways.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the eight rail destinations become icons as the window narrows and the page body stays free of a horizontal scrollbar at every width. No if the rail keeps its labels until the layout breaks, or the page scrolls sideways.

criterion: At phone width the event field reads as inspect-only with the reason stated on the surface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if authoring an overlay is unavailable at phone width with wording that says why, and the replay side panel becomes a bottom sheet keeping its tabs. No if the field offers overlay authoring at phone width, or the side panel disappears.

criterion: Dragging a rectangle across the event field shows an approximate size labelled approximate until the exact figure arrives.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a figure appears during the drag carrying a word marking it approximate, replaced on release by the resolved size, with the marks outside the region dimming. No if the size appears only on release, or the drag figure is presented as exact.

criterion: Zooming across a band boundary on the event field cross-fades the two representations with the field holding data throughout.
evaluation_rule: A band is one of the five drawings of the archive, running from a density image of years to one mark per event. Yes if the outgoing drawing persists until the incoming one has something to show. No if the field goes blank for a frame, or one drawing swaps for the other in one step.

criterion: A dashboard tile whose filter the dashboard overrides carries that override on the tile.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a tile shows which filter is in force when the dashboard filter differs from the tile's own, and a contradiction between the two draws an explicit marker. No if the dashboard quietly resolves the disagreement with nothing shown on the tile.

criterion: A project holding zero events shows the shape the field will take once data arrives, offering the ingest snippet.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the empty field renders a faint procedural texture with wording that says why the project is empty and a control that starts ingest. No if the empty project shows sample events, or offers documentation in place of the snippet.

criterion: A recipient surface whose token stops working holds its last frame as a still image with every control removed.
evaluation_rule: The recipient surface is the shell-free page a share link opens. Yes if the page keeps showing what it last drew, frozen, with one line of text and nothing to press. No if the page shows an error screen, or says which of expiry and revocation happened.
